transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Mark Ruben (Hearthline Procurement); Sofia Alvarez (Hearthline Legal); Derek Cho (Hearthline Platform); Lena Morris (Hearthline FinOps)

Summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA routing (dedicated fallback), pricing approval path; agree to run benchmarks and share artifacts.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call, we have Jordan from Redwood, Priya our solutions engineer, and then Hearthline team?
00:08 Speaker 2 (Mark): Yep Mark here, with Sofia, Derek and Lena.
00:11 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Awesome. Goal for today is to walk through the legal asks in the DPA/MSA, routing and SLA options (hosted vs dedicated vs private deploy), and pricing path for procurement. We'll close with explicit next steps.
00:25 Speaker 3 (Priya): I'll chime in on the technical tradeoffs — we want to show where latency and cost diverge when you pick Dedicated pools vs Hosted API and where Private/VPC matters for keying.
00:33 Speaker 2 (Mark): Good. From procurement we need a clear gating checklist — what legal needs to sign off, what FinOps needs to approve, and any preflight we need to run.

02:07 Speaker 4 (Sofia): Thanks. Couple things from legal: 1) DPA — we need to ensure data residency controls are explicit, 2) subprocessor list and right to audit, 3) KMS key control. We're likely to request customer-managed keys for any PII processing. Also we need SLA definitions to map to our internal RTO/RPO.
02:28 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Understood. On KMS we support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed KMS/HSM for Private deployments; for Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS provider in the VPC flow. There may be an extra engineering touch but that's standard.
02:42 Speaker 4 (Sofia): Also please note we may need to insert a clause about no unapproved subprocessing outside EU/US without notice.

04:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): Quick note, our Dedicated offering gives you predictable throughput, and you get a dedicated GPU pool with isolation. That makes it simpler for egress/egress fee mapping and audit trails — logs from the Dedicated control plane can be shipped to your SIEM or S3. Hosted API is faster to start but has shared infra and has pre-defined subprocessor lists.
04:34 Speaker 5 (Derek): On the platform side we care about latency tail. For customer-facing flows we need p95 ~ 450ms or less. Can your dedicated pool hit that at our expected peak?
04:46 Speaker 3 (Priya): Short answer: yes, but we need your traffic profile. Our microbenchmarks show sub-300ms p95 for similar seq len with Dedicated at the recommended instance count, but p95 depends on batching and KV cache hit rates.
05:00 Speaker 5 (Derek): Right, we'll share token distribution — lots of short bursts with occasional long form generation.

06:20 Speaker 2 (Mark): On pricing: Finance will want a path that starts with hosted credits to validate, then move to committed Dedicated capacity. Need clear pricing breakpoints and cancellation penalties.
06:37 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We typically do a pilot on Hosted (free credits) then sign a Reserved Capacity contract for Dedicated with monthly commit. There's flexibility on burst capacity. We'll put a sample rate card and a scenario-based model in the spreadsheet.
06:50 Speaker 6 (Lena): For FinOps, the biggest question is unit economics at 5M tokens/day. We need to understand cost per 1k tokens on Hosted vs per-hour committed on Dedicated.
07:02 Speaker 3 (Priya): We'll run a simulation with your 5M/day profile — Dedicated usually wins at scale but it depends on sequence length and generation ratio. Quantization and batching configs can shift the crossover point.

09:15 Speaker 4 (Sofia): Back to the DPA, we have a clause about breach notification timelines — 48 hours is our ask. Is that acceptable?
09:27 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Our standard is 72 hours. We can discuss acceleration clauses for customers with stricter needs; for Private deployments we can do shorter windows operationally, but the contract often lands at 72. We can include an exception for regulated data if needed.
09:39 Speaker 4 (Sofia): Hmm... 72 is a bit long for financial data. We'll flag that as a negotiation point.

11:00 Speaker 5 (Derek): Regarding egress — do you charge data egress separately if we hold logs in our S3?
11:07 Speaker 3 (Priya): Egress from Redwood-hosted logging is included up to a limit; however cross-region transfers and external egress into your VPC may show fees. For Dedicated we can often route logs directly into your VPC via private peering to avoid double-charges. We'll outline that in the pricing sheet.

13:40 Speaker 2 (Mark): On onboarding gating: what is the minimal artifact set legal needs to move to approval? SOC2 report, DPA redline acceptance, and an escrow for keys?
13:52 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Minimal usually: SOC2 attestation, signed DPA/MSA, and SSO setup (SAML) for RBAC. Customer-managed KMS is optional but for finance folks it's common. We can also provide runbook and audit logs during onboarding.
14:07 Speaker 4 (Sofia): Does your SOC2 cover Private deployments?
14:12 Speaker 3 (Priya): SOC2 covers Redwood's control plane and hosted infra; Private deployments are supported with customer-managed control plane and we provide a mapping document of responsibilities (shared-resp matrix). For full FedRAMP you'd need a separate pathway — we can discuss that if needed.

16:20 Speaker 6 (Lena): Procurement: what's the SLA credit calculation? Is it per-tenant or per-route? We have multiple lines of business.
16:31 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Great question — credits are per-route or per-configurable service unit. We provide per-route SLOs and token-level breakdowns; credits can be applied per-route so you don't penalize other business units. We'll include that sample SLA matrix.

18:10 Speaker 5 (Derek): Technical question — how do rollouts and fallbacks work if a model variant is down? Can we automatically route to a cheaper/compatible variant?
18:20 Speaker 3 (Priya): Yes, routing policies support per-policy fallbacks: latency first, cost first, region first. You can set canary rollouts, A/B, and automated fallback to compatible variants. We surface traces and error rates in Redwood Console.
18:35 Speaker 5 (Derek): Good. That fallback behavior is important for user-facing endpoints.

20:00 Speaker 4 (Sofia): Regarding subprocessors: we need a current list and a commitment to notify any changes 30 days in advance.
20:09 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We provide a subprocessor CSV and our standard clause is notification, but we can commit to 30 days for major changes. We'll attach the current list to the redline packet.

23:45 Speaker 2 (Mark): A question on indemnity — our legal team wants to limit third-party IP indemnity; what's Redwood's posture?
23:53 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Redwood's standard is mutual indemnity with carve-outs for open model output risks; we'll provide the indemnity section and typical counterproposal language. I expect that's negotiable.

26:10 Speaker 6 (Lena): Pricing approvals: what's the normal internal lead time for approvals once procurement has the rate card?
26:18 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We usually see 1–2 weeks for commercial approval after procurement sees the rate card and commit proposal; for custom enterprise features or KMS integration it can be 2–4 weeks.

28:00 Speaker 3 (Priya): One footnote — when you ask for customer-managed KMS, there are two patterns: fully private deployment with customer control plane (longer set up) or VPC/Dedicated where we integrate with your KMS for envelope keys. Both have different timelines and costs.

30:15 Speaker 5 (Derek): Could you run a quick example of token cost difference? Even ballpark numbers would help procurement.
30:22 Speaker 3 (Priya): Sure. For Hosted base model it's X cents per 1K tokens in our public rate card. For Dedicated, costs translate to $/GPU-hour; when you amortize against QPS and token length you get a break-even. We'll do a scenario with your 5M tokens/day and share the pivot point.
30:40 Speaker 6 (Lena): Please add the assumptions in the sheet (seq len, generation ratio, top-k).

33:00 Speaker 4 (Sofia): A legal nuance — DPA has a data minimization clause that references training data. We want assurance that customer requests and PII won't be used for Redwood model training.
33:14 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Redwood's default is no training on customer data for Hosted customers unless explicitly opted-in; we'll put that in DPA. For Dedicated/Private it's always opt-in if you ask. We'll add explicit language.
33:28 Speaker 4 (Sofia): Great, please sentence that in the redline.

36:05 Speaker 2 (Mark): Onboarding checklist ask: can you provide a sample runbook and a timeline for each onboarding lane (pilot-hosted, pilot-dedicated, full go-live)?
36:15 Speaker 3 (Priya): Yes. We'll share a three-lane runbook: hosted pilot (2–3 weeks), dedicated pilot (4–6 weeks), private/on-prem (8–12 weeks). These are ballparks; exact times depend on KMS, SSO, and test workloads.

38:40 Speaker 5 (Derek): Instrumentation — does Redwood expose token-level logs and traces for debugging? Level of detail?
38:50 Speaker 3 (Priya): Token-level traces are available to the extent you need for debugging. We scrub by default for PII; you can opt-in to raw logs if you run in Dedicated/private lanes with appropriate guardrails and controls.

41:00 Speaker 6 (Lena): For procurement approval, we need to see a sample invoice structure and monthly reconciliation process.
41:09 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We'll include sample invoice templates and reconciliation guidance. Also note we support consolidated billing and per-project cost centers.

44:20 Speaker 2 (Mark): Anything else on SSO? We want SCIM for provisioning and SAML for SSO.
44:28 Speaker 3 (Priya): We support SAML2 and SCIM provisioning. For RBAC we map AD groups to Redwood roles. We can do a test SSO setup during the pilot.

47:15 Speaker 4 (Sofia): One more legal ask — audit window. We need logs retained for 2 years. Is that feasible?
47:23 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Default retention is 90 days in the Console; extended retention is an add-on we can provide (up to multi-year retention) and can be routed to your S3 bucket for long-term archival. We'll include retention pricing.

50:30 Speaker 5 (Derek): A small technical clarification: do you maintain KV cache warmers or is cache cold on a model switch?
50:38 Speaker 3 (Priya): Warmers exist via prefix caching; when you switch model variants you lose some KV cache unless you use compatible variants and preserve key shapes. We'll include a note in the runbook.

53:05 Speaker 2 (Mark): Recap before we close — legal wants DPA redline, SOC2 artifacts, subprocessors list; tech wants token distribution and perf microbenchmarks; finance wants rate card + invoice sample. Is that right?
53:18 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Correct. To add: Priya will produce a dedicated vs hosted pivot spreadsheet. We'll shoot all artifacts into the shared drive and follow up by email.

55:00 Speaker 4 (Sofia): We'll review redline and come back with priority list. Also note we'll push any non-starter clauses early.
55:10 Speaker 6 (Lena): Please call out the cost crossover point explicitly. We need that for our internal pricing committee.

58:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Okay thanks everyone. Quick timeline: we'll share the MSA/DPA redline digest and the rate-card spreadsheet by next Tuesday 2025-05-12. Priya will run the benchmark and circulate results by 2025-05-14. Derek, please drop the traffic/Profile by 2025-05-13. Any final comments?
58:21 Speaker 5 (Derek): No, thanks. That's good.
58:26 Speaker 2 (Mark): Thanks all.
58:30 Speaker 4 (Sofia): Thanks.
58:33 Speaker 3 (Priya): Thanks, bye.
58:35 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Bye everyone.
